title: Tortilla Espanola
subtitle: Spanish potato and egg omelette
excerpt: A thick, set omelette of thinly sliced potato and onion cooked slowly in olive oil, then bound with beaten egg. The potatoes are not fried until crisp; they are confit-poached in olive oil until tender before the egg goes in, which gives the inside a soft, almost creamy texture. Served warm, at room temperature or cold, it works at any time of day.
sourceNotes: The Spanish tortilla has been documented since at least the 19th century; it is the most widely eaten dish in Spain and served at any time of day, from breakfast through to late-night tapas.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tortilla is arguably better at room temperature than straight from the pan. Cook up to 4 hours ahead and leave covered at room temperature.

content.text: The flip is the hardest part. You need a plate slightly wider than your pan. When the bottom is set and the top is still slightly wobbly, place the plate over the pan, hold both firmly and flip in one confident motion. Slide the tortilla back into the pan to set the second side. Hesitating mid-flip is the main cause of disaster, so commit fully. A non-stick pan makes the whole process considerably easier.

items.prepNote: peeled and thinly sliced, about 3mm thick

content.text: Pour the olive oil into a 26cm frying pan over a medium-low heat. Add the sliced potato and onion with a generous pinch of salt. They should be just submerged. Cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are completely tender but not coloured. This is a poach in oil, not a fry.

Drain the potato and onion through a sieve set over a bowl. Reserve the oil. Beat the eggs in a large bowl with salt and pepper. Add the drained potato and onion to the eggs, press them gently and leave to soak for 5 minutes.

Return 2 tablespoons of the reserved oil to the pan over a medium heat. Pour in the egg and potato mixture, spreading it evenly. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the edges are set and only the centre is slightly wobbly.

Place a large plate over the pan. Hold both firmly and flip in one confident move. Add another tablespoon of oil to the pan, then slide the tortilla back in, cooked-side up. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until set through. Slide onto a plate and rest for at least 5 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: Tortilla fell apart during the flip
items.cause: The first side was not set enough before flipping, or the plate was too small
items.fix: Use a plate at least 2cm wider than the pan and only flip when the sides are completely set. The centre can be slightly wobbly but the edges must be firm.

items.symptom: Centre is raw after flipping back into the pan
items.cause: Eggs were not at room temperature or the second side was not cooked long enough
items.fix: Cover the pan with a lid for the last 2 minutes of cooking. The trapped heat will set the centre without drying out the outside.
